summary:
Task 2 (auto-install-transaction) is feasible inside its two scope files using the real APIs. I checked it end to end with a scratch prototype in a temp dir, outside the repo. The prototype built an installed record from automationSchedulePlan output plus name, trigger, timeZone, a random installationId and an ISO installedAt. It initialized ledgers with initializeAutomationDispatch(join(root,'runtime'), record) and wrote the same object to root/installed/<name>.json. runInstalledAutomation then returned status 'succeeded'. Adding one extra field to the installed file after the ledger was made gave 'invalid_state', because the dispatch ledger binds a digest of the whole record (dispatch.mjs:26,72). An in-process same-name race is refused by an exclusive 'wx' intent file: a second call got EEXIST and createDisabled was called once. A publication failure can be injected with no fs hooks by making root/runtime a regular file, which gives ENOTDIR (the prototype recorded publication_failed). The 7 existing automation suites pass at HEAD (82/82).

Hazards specific to this task:
(1) plan.policy has neither `trigger` nor the bare `name`. plan.name is 'orion-auto-<name>', and the runtime looks up installed/<proposal.name>.json.
(2) The transaction file must keep the full plan and record. Task 3's reconcile({root,name,scheduler}) gets no proposal or repoRoot, so it cannot rebuild the expected plan.
(3) The harness marks a check UNUSABLE, and blocks the task for a human, if the first 2000 chars of its output contain ENOENT, 'No such file or directory' or 'command not found'. That includes a test title or failure message (checks.mjs:189-191, worker.mjs:319-323).
(4) With the 6 context files plus 2 scope files the working set is at its limit of 8. The scope files load first and are evicted first. A 9th READ drops the install module, and the model would then rewrite it blind and lose task 1's verifyDisabledSchedule.
(5) After the first write, the stuck gate allows about 3 more write/check exchanges before handing the task to the reviewer.

The contract leaves these open, and none needs Astra: the type and requiredness of `now`, the return shape of createDisabled, throw versus return on failure, the path and schema of the intent file, whether remove() is used, and the classification of a failed read-back.

The code's nextGate string (schedule.mjs:30) orders ledgers before job creation. The contract objective orders publication after verification. Follow the contract.

Brief budget: common.md plus this task's brief must total 18,000 characters or less (contract.mjs:65, plan.mjs:70-71).

Host-side facts come from the uncommitted working copy of scripts/lib/agentic/*, which is what the running host loads. HEAD differs: HEAD's checks.mjs does not register 'automation-install-tests', and HEAD's worker has no 12000-char large-write trigger.

apis.name: automationSchedulePlan
apis.signature: automationSchedulePlan(proposal, timeZone, repoRoot, now = Date.now()) -> plan (sync, throws Error)
apis.behavior: Pure. Runs validateProposal with expiresOn swapped for real-clock tomorrow, then throws the joined issues (9-11). Throws unless action==='agenda_today' and delivery===undefined (12-14). Throws 'An explicit IANA timezone...' on an invalid zone or policy (15-18). Throws 'Invalid current clock' unless now is a safe integer >= 0; a Date object or function throws (19). Throws /Expiry/ unless expiresOn falls from today through 180 days ahead in timeZone, with today computed from `now`, not the real clock (20-25). Returns {readyToInstall:false, nextGate, name:`orion-auto-${proposal.name}`, timeZone, cron, commandArgv:[join(repoRoot,'scripts/orion-automation-run'), proposal.name], policy:{action,intent,expiresOn,conditions,permissions,riskLimits,failureBehavior}, schedulerArgs:[... '--command-cwd', repoRoot, '--disabled','--exact','--no-deliver', ...]} (27-40). policy has NO trigger, name, timeZone or installationId (32-34). Touches no files and spawns nothing.

apis.name: initializeAutomationDispatch
apis.signature: async initializeAutomationDispatch(root, value) -> undefined; throws on invalid record or existing ledger
apis.behavior: installation(value) canonicalizes the record and requires action in AUTOMATION_ACTIONS, failureBehavior in {stop,retry_once,report_and_continue}, installationId a string and a valid trigger; binding = sha256(canonical(record)), key = sha256(installationId) (14-27). Calls initializeAutomationAdmission(join(root,'admission'), record), which does mkdir recursive 0o700 and an exclusive 'wx' write (52; admission.mjs:64-70). Initializes messages only if record.delivery is set (53). Writes root/<key>.dispatch.json exclusively ('wx', initial=true) as {version:1,binding,phase:'ready',lastAt:null,lastSlot:null}, then fsyncs the file and directory (39-49, 54-56). Calling it again throws EEXIST. When root is a regular file it throws ENOTDIR (both observed in the prototype). No rollback: if the admission write succeeds and the dispatch write fails, the admission ledger stays.

apis.name: dispatchAutomation
apis.signature: async dispatchAutomation(root, value, scheduledAt, adapters) -> {status, reason?, ...}
apis.behavior: Refuses with 'invalid_state' when ledger.binding !== sha256(canonical(record)) (72-77). The installed record and the record passed to initializeAutomationDispatch must therefore be canonically identical. Keys are sorted (11-12), so key order does not matter, but any added or changed field does.

apis.name: initializeAutomationAdmission / binding
apis.behavior: binding() throws unless name matches /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,47}$/, installationId matches /^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{8,80}$/ (randomUUID() satisfies this), expiresOn is a valid day, riskLimits.maxRunsPerDay is 1-1440, permissions.expectsMode is a known mode, conditions is an object, and timeZone is 'UTC' or in Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') (14-29). The binding hash covers name, installationId, timeZone, expiresOn, maxRunsPerDay, expectsMode, quietHours and skipDuringFocus (30-40). Ledger file: root/<sha256(installationId)>.json = {version:1,binding,day:null,runs:0,lastAt:0}, written 'wx' with mode 0o600 (42-50, 64-70). writeNew and syncDirectory are NOT exported (46-54).

apis.name: checkAutomationConditions
apis.behavior: Checks conditions only and never throws: 'invalid_policy' on a bad record. The task 2 implementation does not need it; the plan already uses it (schedule.mjs:16).

apis.name: runInstalledAutomation
apis.signature: async runInstalledAutomation(name, scheduledAt, {automationRoot = ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/automations, repoRoot = repo, checks = createAutomationHostChecks({repoRoot}), run = execFile} = {})
apis.behavior: Has PRODUCTION DEFAULTS (19-20): tests must always pass automationRoot, repoRoot, checks and run. Reads join(automationRoot,'installed',`${name}.json`) (25). Refuses 'installation_unavailable_or_unsupported' unless record.name===name, action==='agenda_today', delivery===undefined and installedAt is a Date.parse-able string (28-34). Requires action.installationId === record.installationId (51) and dispatches at join(automationRoot,'runtime') (77). A missing ledger is refused and never recreated (runtime.test.mjs:62-65).

apis.name: validateProposal / NAME_RE / MAX_AUTOMATION_DAYS / AUTOMATION_ACTIONS / cronExpression
apis.signature: validateProposal(value) -> string[]; NAME_RE (104); MAX_AUTOMATION_DAYS = 180 (106); AUTOMATION_ACTIONS (76-102); cronExpression(trigger) (209-218)
apis.behavior: Rejects an invalid name, intent under 8 chars, a bad trigger shape, unknown action, bad quietHours, bad expiresOn, maxRunsPerDay outside 1-1440, maxMessagesPerDay outside 0-48, bad failureBehavior or bad expectsMode. Does NOT reject extra top-level or trigger keys (schedule.test.mjs:13 adds `command`, which is ignored). Tracked at HEAD, so the import works in the worktree.

apis.name: verifyDisabledSchedule (task 1, not yet written)
apis.behavior: Required by task 1's acceptance (plan md:87-88). expected = automationSchedulePlan output. observed = {id,name,timeZone,cron,commandArgv,cwd,enabled,exact,noDeliver}. true only for a nonempty id, exact name/timeZone/cron/argv, cwd equal to the '--command-cwd' value in schedulerArgs, enabled===false, exact===true and noDeliver===true. Pure. Task 2 must re-read the actual code, call it, treat only `=== true` as verified, and keep its export and tests unchanged.

apis.name: removeAutomationSchedule (legacy CLI helper; not to be used by task 2)
apis.behavior: Spawns the real openclaw CLI through `run`. Shown only as prior art for 'no success claim without read-back'. Task 2 must NOT import it; its scheduler access goes only through the injected adapter.

apis.name: orion-automation CLI install/remove (context, out of scope)
apis.behavior: The only current writer of installed/ (comment at 21-25). ROOT is ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/automations (57-59). remove deletes installedAt and cron, rewrites the record to proposed/ and unlinks installed/<name>.json (173-177). It knows nothing about transaction files, installationId or ledgers. Out of scope for task 2.

apis.name: runCheck / environmentBroken (host)
apis.signature: environmentBroken(result) = startFailure || exit 127 || /command not found|ENOENT|No such file or directory/i on the first 2000 chars of output
apis.behavior: This flag is set even on a PASSING run. worker.mjs:319-323 then throws WorkerBlocked({humanOnly:true}). automation-install-tests is registered at checks.mjs:63-68 (working copy only; HEAD lacks it). automation-tests is registered at 69-77. node-syntax runs `node --check` on each changed .mjs/.js file (37-43).

apis.name: worker loop constants (host)
apis.behavior: Initial working set = the existing scope files (73-81). A READ appends and splices the OLDEST entries past 8 (261). A FILE write updates an existing entry in place without moving it (282-284). The first write of a path in an attempt counts as progress (277). A write over 12000 chars triggers a one-time self-review (280). A check going fail->pass counts as progress (306); a pass<->fail change triggers a self-review (307-310); the same failure twice triggers a self-review (312-315). barren += 1 on every turn with a write, CHECK or DONE (342-343); >= 4 means stuck (344-353). DONE is refused while triggers are pending (355) or checks are stale (360). A checkpoint withholds DONE (195-205).

apis.name: fitWorkingSet / promptBudget (host)
apis.behavior: Drops the oldest files until the estimate of bytes/3 fits 65536 - 16000 - 1024 = 48512 tokens (30, 33, 46-55; models.mjs:59,63). The worker's output cap is 16000 tokens (models.mjs:63).

shapes.name: automationSchedulePlan output (the `plan` / verifier `expected`)
shapes.definition: { readyToInstall:false, nextGate:string, name:'orion-auto-'+proposal.name, timeZone, cron:string, commandArgv:[<repoRoot>/scripts/orion-automation-run, proposal.name], policy:{action,intent,expiresOn,conditions,permissions,riskLimits,failureBehavior}, schedulerArgs:['cron','add','--name',name,'--cron',cron,'--tz',timeZone,'--command-argv',JSON.stringify(commandArgv),'--command-cwd',repoRoot,'--disabled','--exact','--no-deliver','--timeout-seconds','120','--output-max-bytes','4096','--json'] }. JSON-safe, so it can be persisted verbatim in the transaction file.
shapes.evidence: scripts/lib/orion-automation-schedule.mjs:28-40; observed output of the prototype run

shapes.name: Installed record at root/installed/<proposal.name>.json (as consumed by runInstalledAutomation)
shapes.definition: { name: proposal.name (NOT plan.name), installationId: randomUUID() (fits /^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{8,80}$/), installedAt: new Date(now).toISOString(), timeZone, trigger: {kind, atMinute, atHour?, weekday?} copied from proposal.trigger, ...plan.policy (action, intent, expiresOn, conditions, permissions, riskLimits, failureBehavior) }. delivery must be absent. The exact same object must go to initializeAutomationDispatch and to the file.
shapes.evidence: runtime.mjs:25,29-30,51; dispatch.mjs:14-27 (trigger, failureBehavior, installationId required); admission.mjs:14-29; fixture tests/automation-runtime.test.mjs:13-16; prototype run returned status 'succeeded'

shapes.name: Admission (runs) ledger
shapes.definition: root/runtime/admission/<sha256hex(installationId)>.json = {version:1, binding:<policy hash>, day:null, runs:0, lastAt:0}. A messages ledger exists only when delivery is set, which never happens for agenda_today without delivery.

shapes.name: Scheduler adapter (injected)
shapes.definition: { createDisabled(plan) -> returns the new job id (the contract does not fix string vs {id}; pick one and validate that it is a nonempty string), read(id) -> normalized observed {id,name,timeZone,cron,commandArgv,cwd,enabled,exact,noDeliver}, remove(id) }. There is no enable method, and task 2 never calls one.
shapes.evidence: plan md:133 (task 2 acceptance 1), md:87 (task 1 observed shape)

shapes.name: Transaction intent (NOT specified by the contract; recommended)
shapes.definition: A deterministic per-name path under root, outside installed/, runtime/ and proposed/, e.g. root/transactions/<name>.json. Create it with open(...,'wx',0o600) and fsync the file and directory BEFORE createDisabled. Suggested content: {version:1, name, state, installationId, installedAt, timeZone, schedulerId:null|string, plan:<full plan>, record:<full installed record>}. Later updates go through temp file + rename + directory fsync, safe because this process owns the name. Suggested state values separate the three classes the contract names. No effect: failed before create was called. Unknown scheduler outcome: 'creating' with schedulerId null, which is also what a crash leaves, or create threw or returned an invalid id. Known job: schedulerId recorded, then verified or readback_failed, then publication_failed or installed. Task 3's reconcile({root,name,scheduler}) must find everything here by name alone.
shapes.evidence: plan md:135 (intent before scheduler effect), md:136 (distinguish no effect / known disabled job / unknown outcome), md:186-189 (task 3 needs transaction identity + read-back, gets only root/name/scheduler); existing durable-write idiom admission.mjs:46-54, dispatch.mjs:39-49

shapes.definition: { name:'calendar-check', intent:'Read the calendar at the chosen time', action:'agenda_today', expiresOn, trigger:{kind:'daily',atHour:9,atMinute:5}, conditions:{}, permissions:{expectsMode:'guarded'}, riskLimits:{maxRunsPerDay:2,maxMessagesPerDay:0}, failureBehavior:'stop' }

criteria.criterion: Export installDisabledAutomation({root,proposal,timeZone,repoRoot,scheduler,now}); all roots and scheduler adapters are required, with no implicit production defaults. scheduler exposes createDisabled(plan), read(id), remove(id). This function never enables a job.
criteria.approach: Add `export async function installDisabledAutomation({ root, proposal, timeZone, repoRoot, scheduler, now } = {})`. Before any effect: throw unless root and repoRoot are nonempty (preferably absolute) strings, and unless scheduler is an object whose createDisabled, read and remove are all functions. No homedir(), no repo-relative default, no default scheduler. Do not import child_process. Call only scheduler.createDisabled and scheduler.read. Nothing enables a job, and the plan handed over contains '--disabled'. Pass `now` straight to automationSchedulePlan, which demands a safe integer (schedule.mjs:19). Tests: each missing argument throws with zero scheduler calls and no files under root. A recording fake shows only create and read were called, and the plan it received deepEquals an independently computed automationSchedulePlan(proposal, tz, repoRoot, now) and includes '--disabled'.
criteria.evidence: Production-default anti-pattern to avoid: runtime.mjs:19-20, host.mjs:23-24, scripts/orion-automation:57-60. Plan contents: schedule.mjs:36-39.
criteria.risk: Copying runtime.mjs's `= join(homedir(), ...)` defaults. Defaulting repoRoot to the repo path. Validating only root and forgetting repoRoot or scheduler methods. Treating `now` as a function (Date.now), which makes the plan throw 'Invalid current clock'.

criteria.criterion: Use automationSchedulePlan, a new random installationId, installation-bound timezone/installedAt, and initializeAutomationDispatch at root/runtime. Publish the installed record at root/installed/<name>.json in the shape consumed by runInstalledAutomation.
criteria.approach: plan = automationSchedulePlan(proposal, timeZone, repoRoot, now), called before any path uses proposal.name, since the plan validates the name against '../' (schedule.test.mjs:43). record = { name: proposal.name, installationId: randomUUID(), installedAt: new Date(now).toISOString(), timeZone, trigger: <proposal.trigger kind/atHour/atMinute/weekday>, ...plan.policy }. Build it once and persist it in the intent. After verification call initializeAutomationDispatch(join(root,'runtime'), record), then publish exactly the same object to join(root,'installed',`${proposal.name}.json`). Publish exclusively: write a temp file 'wx' 0o600, fsync, link() to the final name (EEXIST means refuse), unlink the temp, fsync the directory. Do NOT use rename, which overwrites. Tests: parse the installed file and check the fields; check that runtime/<sha256(installationId)>.dispatch.json has phase 'ready'; optionally run runInstalledAutomation once with injected options and expect 'succeeded'.
criteria.evidence: runtime.mjs:25,28-34,77; dispatch.mjs:14-27,50-57,72; admission.mjs:16,26-29; runtime.test.mjs:13-20; prototype returned status 'succeeded', and an extra field gave 'invalid_state'
criteria.risk: Using plan.name ('orion-auto-x') as the filename or record.name, so the runtime refuses. Omitting trigger, which plan.policy lacks, so dispatch throws 'invalid trigger'. Adding fields such as schedulerId or cron to the installed file after the ledger exists, which gives an 'invalid_state' binding mismatch. Hand-writing ledger JSON instead of calling initializeAutomationDispatch. Spreading the whole proposal, which carries stray fields like `command`. Using 'preview-only' or any fixed id.

criteria.criterion: Persist an exclusive per-name transaction intent before any scheduler effect; prevent overwrite of existing installation, ledger, or uncertain transaction. Record returned scheduler id before proceeding to verifyDisabledSchedule.
criteria.approach: (a) Refuse before writing anything if installed/<name>.json exists. Treat only ENOENT as absent; any other error means refuse. (b) mkdir root/transactions recursively with 0o700, create the intent with open('wx') holding state 'creating', schedulerId null, the full plan and the full record, then fsync the file and directory. EEXIST means refuse, which covers both a concurrent same-name call and any earlier transaction, completed or uncertain. (c) Call createDisabled with a structuredClone of the plan. (d) If it throws or returns a non-string or empty id, durably mark 'create outcome unknown' and fail. (e) Otherwise durably write schedulerId (temp + rename + directory fsync) BEFORE calling read(id). Ledgers cannot be overwritten because the admission and dispatch writes are 'wx' (admission.mjs:47, dispatch.mjs:40-42) and the installationId is new. Never delete or overwrite the intent in a cleanup path.
criteria.evidence: admission.mjs:46-54 and dispatch.mjs:39-49 show the durable-write idiom (neither helper is exported, so it must be re-implemented locally); dispatch.test.mjs:28-33 shows the check-disk-at-call-time pattern; prototype second-call result was EEXIST with create calls = 1
criteria.risk: Checking existence and then writing without 'wx' (a race). A `finally { unlink(intent) }` that erases evidence or deletes another caller's intent. Recording the id only in memory, or after read(). Writing the intent after createDisabled. Putting the intent inside installed/, which the legacy CLI lists as 'running' (scripts/orion-automation:92,100-103). Storing only the id: task 3 cannot rebuild the expected plan, because reconcile gets no proposal or repoRoot.

criteria.criterion: Return verified disabled state only after durable policy/ledger publication and exact read-back. Errors preserve enough durable status to distinguish no effect, known disabled job, and unknown scheduler outcome.
criteria.approach: Order: intent, create, persist id, observed = await read(id), verifyDisabledSchedule(plan, observed) === true, persist 'verified', initializeAutomationDispatch, publish the installed record, persist 'installed', return something like {status:'installed_disabled', verified:true, enabled:false, name, installationId, schedulerId}. Failure classes, all recorded durably and never returned as success. Nothing written, or intent marked no-effect, when failure comes before create is called. Unknown when create threw or returned an invalid id, and also when 'creating' is left behind by a crash. Known job id when read threw or the verifier returned false: record schedulerId plus the observed value, and do NOT call remove or anything else. Known verified disabled job when publication failed: record schedulerId, installationId and the error class; ledgers may be partial and the installed record is absent. A second read-back after publication is allowed but not required by the literal text.
criteria.evidence: plan md:127 (objective: publish only after verifying), md:136; md:187-188 (task 3 owns cleanup and uncertain states); dispatch.mjs:50-57 (partial ledger possible: admission is written before dispatch)
criteria.risk: Returning success before the installed record is published and fsynced. Labeling a failed read-back as 'known disabled' when disabled-ness was never established. Calling remove(id) after a mismatch, which could touch a job that is not ours; task 3 forbids changing unrelated jobs. Swallowing errors and returning a success-shaped object. Error messages that leak raw fs errors with 'ENOENT' into test output.

criteria.criterion: Tests show successful disabled registration, same-name concurrency refusal, unchanged existing record, failure before create, failed read-back, and failure during publication. Existing policy checks are never replaced with unconditional authorization.
criteria.approach: Add all of these to tests/automation-install.test.mjs and keep every task 1 test. (1) Success: verified result; installed file fields; dispatch ledger phase 'ready'; the transaction file shows installed plus schedulerId; the fake saw create then read in that order and never anything else; optionally runInstalledAutomation with fully injected options returns 'succeeded'. (2) Concurrency: 8 calls through Promise.allSettled; exactly 1 verified; createDisabled called once. (3) Existing record: pre-write installed/<name>.json; install refused; bytes identical; no create call; no runtime ledger created. Also cover a second install over a completed or uncertain transaction file: refused, file unchanged. (4) Failure before create: an invalid proposal or timezone, or root being a regular file; zero create calls; no installed or runtime files. (5) Failed read-back: read returns an independently built observed object with one field wrong (e.g. enabled:true or a different cwd), plus a variant where read throws; no installed record; no runtime directory; the transaction keeps schedulerId; remove not called. (6) Publication failure: root/runtime is a regular file; read-back was verified; installed record absent; the transaction records the known job and the failed publication. The implementation never writes ledger phases or authorization directly.
criteria.evidence: dispatch.test.mjs:59-63 (concurrency pattern); runtime.test.mjs:23-38 (injected checks are the established pattern); prototype (ENOTDIR injection)
criteria.risk: A fake read that echoes the plan it was given, so verification always passes (the 'validate an object against itself' trap from task 1). Promise.all rejecting early while the winner still writes into a root that t.after is deleting. Test titles or failure output containing 'ENOENT' or 'No such file or directory', which the harness treats as a broken environment. Using chmod-based failures, which do not fail when run as root. Using Date.now() with a literal expiresOn, which breaks after that date. Omitting runtime options so the real home directory is used.

issues.detail: `now` is listed in the signature, but its type and whether it is required are unstated. The contract says only 'all roots and scheduler adapters are required'.
issues.evidence: plan md:133; automationSchedulePlan takes a numeric `now` defaulting to Date.now() and rejects non-integers (schedule.mjs:6,19); host checks and tick use a function (host.mjs:24, tick.mjs:5)
issues.contractText: Export installDisabledAutomation({root,proposal,timeZone,repoRoot,scheduler,now}); all roots and scheduler adapters are required
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Treat `now` as epoch milliseconds (a safe integer), passed unchanged to automationSchedulePlan and used for installedAt = new Date(now).toISOString(). Requiring it (throw if absent) and defaulting it to Date.now() both satisfy the text, because it is neither a root nor an adapter. Tests must always pass a fixed value.

issues.detail: The return shape of createDisabled(plan) is unspecified: a bare id string, or an object containing id.
issues.evidence: plan md:133,135 ('Record returned scheduler id'); observed has `id` (md:87)
issues.contractText: scheduler exposes createDisabled(plan), read(id), remove(id)... Record returned scheduler id before proceeding to verifyDisabledSchedule.
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Choose one form, document it in a comment next to the function, and have tasks 3 and 4 reuse it. Accept only a nonempty string id; anything else is an 'unknown scheduler outcome' and gets no retry. Either form is faithful.

issues.detail: It is not specified whether failures throw or return a status object. 'Errors' suggests throwing. What the contract does fix is the durable status.
issues.evidence: plan md:136; existing modules mix both styles: plan throws (schedule.mjs:11,13,18,19,25), runtime and dispatch return {status,reason} (runtime.mjs:23,34; dispatch.mjs:62-63)
issues.contractText: Errors preserve enough durable status to distinguish no effect, known disabled job, and unknown scheduler outcome.
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Either is acceptable as long as a failure can never be mistaken for the verified result, and every failure test asserts the on-disk transaction state as well as the thrown or returned value. Invalid arguments should throw before any effect.

issues.detail: The path and schema of the transaction intent are unspecified. Task 3's reconcile({root,name,scheduler}) has no proposal, timeZone, repoRoot or now, so it can only verify exact identity if task 2 persists the expected plan and record.
issues.evidence: plan md:135 (task 2), md:186-189 (task 3 signature and needs)
issues.contractText: Persist an exclusive per-name transaction intent before any scheduler effect
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Use a deterministic per-name file under root that is not in installed/, runtime/ or proposed/ (e.g. root/transactions/<name>.json). Create it with 'wx'. Include version, name, state, installationId, installedAt, timeZone, schedulerId, the full plan and the full record. The legacy CLI treats every *.json in installed/ as a running automation (scripts/orion-automation:74-86,100-103), so the intent must not go there.

issues.detail: The contract's ordering disagrees with the in-code nextGate string, which says to publish ledgers BEFORE creating the job. The contract objective says to publish only AFTER verifying.
issues.evidence: schedule.mjs:30 ('publish installation identity and durable ledgers, create disabled job, verify it, then enable it'); HEAD docs/planning/v2/PHASE_57_SCHEDULE_2026-09-21.md:50-52; plan md:127
issues.contractText: Add an injected-host installation transaction that publishes compatible policy and ledgers only after verifying the disabled scheduler job.
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Follow the contract. The intent carries the installation identity before create (which satisfies 'identity first'), and the ledgers plus installed record are published only after verifyDisabledSchedule returns true. Do not edit the nextGate string: schedule.mjs is out of scope.

issues.detail: There are three named classes, but a failed read-back (id known, disabled state not established) is neither 'no effect' nor a verified 'known disabled job'.
issues.evidence: plan md:136; md:188 ('Mismatched or unexpectedly enabled jobs are reported for intervention')
issues.contractText: distinguish no effect, known disabled job, and unknown scheduler outcome
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Record the facts rather than a label: schedulerId known, verified false, the observed value or read error kept as evidence. Never mark a failed read-back as disabled. Task 3 decides what to do with it.

issues.detail: remove(id) is part of the required adapter, but no task 2 criterion says when to call it.
issues.evidence: plan md:133; task 3 limits removal to exact identity plus matching read-back (md:188)
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Validate that remove is a function, but do not call it in task 2. Leave jobs after failed read-back or failed publication for reconciliation, with durable evidence. Calling remove after a mismatched read-back could change a job that is not ours.

issues.detail: 'Existing policy checks are never replaced with unconditional authorization' could be misread as forbidding injected `authorize: async () => true` in tests, which the existing runtime suite uses.

The installer must not write ledger phases, bypass initializeAutomationDispatch, change runtime or admission modules, or add any code path that authorizes. Injected host-check fakes in tests, as the runtime suite already uses, remain acceptable.

issues.detail: No registered check can detect durability (fsync of file and directory), the absence of production defaults, the absence of child_process/spawn in the installer, never-enables beyond the fake's surface, or the exclusive publish (link vs rename). automation-tests only proves the existing suites still pass.

issues.contractText: all roots and scheduler adapters are required, with no implicit production defaults ... This function never enables a job ... durable policy/ledger publication
issues.recommendedInterpretation: The reviewer must read the diff for these (see reviewerChecks). Tests can cover part of it: missing-argument throws, a recording fake with only three methods, and intent and id on disk at call time.

issues.detail: Harness hazard: a check's output that matches /command not found|ENOENT|No such file or directory/i in its first 2000 chars is classified UNUSABLE even when it passed, and the task is blocked humanOnly. In this task, ENOENT is the natural failure of reading a transaction or installed file that was not written.

issues.detail: The legacy human CLI's remove path (scripts/orion-automation) is out of scope. It knows nothing about the new transaction file or ledgers: it moves the installed record to proposed/ and deletes only installedAt and cron, leaving installationId, timeZone and trigger in the proposal. Once an installed record is removed that way, a new install of the same name is refused forever by the leftover transaction file.
issues.evidence: scripts/orion-automation:159-179 (173-177); plan md:307 lists connecting the CLI as next-batch work
issues.contractText: prevent overwrite of existing installation, ledger, or uncertain transaction
issues.recommendedInterpretation: Task 2 must not touch scripts/orion-automation (out of scope, and a forbidden script per its header, lines 21-25). Note it as a known limitation for task 5's packet and the next batch. The refuse-on-existing-transaction behavior is the conservative reading.

issues.detail: The contract's context string abbreviates paths ('orion-automation-dispatch.mjs, orion-automation-admission.mjs, orion-automation-runtime.mjs'). READ needs repo-relative full paths, so a bare name fails.

issues.contractText: Read scripts/lib/orion-automation-schedule.mjs, orion-automation-dispatch.mjs, orion-automation-admission.mjs, orion-automation-runtime.mjs and tests/automation-schedule.test.mjs.
issues.recommendedInterpretation: The brief lists the full paths: scripts/lib/orion-automation-{schedule,dispatch,admission,runtime}.mjs, tests/automation-schedule.test.mjs, tests/automation-runtime.test.mjs.

pitfalls: WORKING-SET EVICTION DROPS TASK 1'S CODE: the scope files are loaded first (worker.mjs:73-81), and a READ past 8 files splices the OLDEST (worker.mjs:261). A FILE write updates in place without moving the file to the end (282-284). The 6 context files plus 2 scope files is exactly 8. A 9th READ (plugin dist, host.mjs, dispatch test) evicts scripts/lib/orion-automation-install.mjs, and the next full-file write then drops verifyDisabledSchedule and its tests. Read only the 6 context files; the brief supplies everything else.

Rewriting the whole module or test file and losing task 1's `verifyDisabledSchedule` export or any task 1 test. Both files must be returned complete, containing everything already in them plus the additions.

Using plan.name ('orion-auto-<name>') for the installed filename or record.name. The runtime reads installed/<proposal.name>.json and requires record.name === name (runtime.mjs:25,29). The tick passes proposal.name (schedule.mjs:27).
Building the record from plan.policy alone: it has no `trigger`, `name`, `timeZone`, `installationId` or `installedAt` (schedule.mjs:32-34), so dispatch throws 'invalid trigger' (dispatch.mjs:19-22).

Passing one object to initializeAutomationDispatch and writing a different one (extra schedulerId, cron, readyToInstall, a differently cloned trigger with extra keys) to installed/. Binding = sha256(canonical(record)) (dispatch.mjs:26), so the runtime gets 'invalid_state' (dispatch.mjs:72). Build the record once and use that same object for both writes.

Validating an object against itself: a fake read() that returns fields copied from the plan it received (or from the same object) always verifies. Construct the observed object in the test from literal expected values (e.g. commandArgv: [join(repoRoot,'scripts/orion-automation-run'), 'calendar-check'], cwd: repoRoot). For failed read-back, change one field. Also pass structuredClone(plan) to createDisabled, so a mutating adapter cannot change the expected value the verifier sees.

Writing the intent AFTER createDisabled, or recording schedulerId only in memory, or after read(). Prove the order with fakes that read the transaction file at call time (the dispatch.test.mjs:28-33 pattern).
A cleanup `finally` that unlinks the intent or transaction file. That destroys the evidence the contract requires, and after an EEXIST refusal it deletes the OTHER caller's intent.

Using rename() to publish installed/<name>.json: rename overwrites. Use an exclusive create (open 'wx') or temp + link() (link fails with EEXIST). Durable means handle.sync() on the file and a sync of the directory, as in admission.mjs:46-54.

Calling scheduler.remove after a failed read-back or failed publication. The contract does not ask for it, and task 3 restricts removal to exact identity plus a matching read-back. Also never call any enable-like method.

Production paths and processes: copying runtime.mjs's defaults (homedir automations root, repo root, createAutomationHostChecks, execFile; runtime.mjs:19-20). In tests, calling runInstalledAutomation without automationRoot/repoRoot/checks/run reads the real ~/.openclaw. Never import child_process in the installer. Never import removal.mjs.

Trying to import non-exported helpers (writeNew and syncDirectory in admission.mjs:46-54; persist in dispatch.mjs:39). ESM fails at link time with 'does not provide an export named', and every test in the file fails. Write small local helpers instead.
Using proposal.name in a path before automationSchedulePlan has validated it. '../outside' is rejected by the plan (schedule.test.mjs:43). Compute the plan first.

Using `now: Date.now` (a function) or a Date object: the plan throws 'Invalid current clock' (schedule.mjs:19). Using Date.now() in tests with a literal expiresOn: the test breaks when the calendar passes that date. Use fixed now = Date.parse('2026-09-20T09:00:00Z') with expiresOn '2026-09-27'. Timezone: expiry is judged in the chosen zone (schedule.mjs:20-25), and 'UTC' is accepted explicitly (admission.mjs:27). Non-canonical aliases such as 'EST' are rejected (schedule.test.mjs:47).

HARNESS TRAP: any 'ENOENT', 'No such file or directory' or 'command not found' in the first 2000 chars of a check's output makes the check UNUSABLE and the task blocked for a human, even on a pass (checks.mjs:189-191, worker.mjs:319-323). Do not put these words in test titles. Read files in tests with `readFile(f,'utf8').then(JSON.parse, () => null)`. Wrap fs errors in your own messages. Inject failures with a regular file where a directory is expected: that gives ENOTDIR, which is safe.

Promise.all in the concurrency test: if refusals throw, Promise.all rejects early while the winner is still writing, and t.after deletes the root under it, making the test flaky. Use Promise.allSettled and assert exactly one verified result and exactly one createDisabled call.
Deferred or gated fakes without a timeout can hang the check until its 5-minute limit (checks.mjs:63-68). Prefer the Promise.allSettled pattern with no gate, or give the test { timeout: 10000 }.
Treating any access or stat error as 'not installed'. Only ENOENT means absent; ENOTDIR, EACCES and others must refuse with no effect.
Permission-based failure injection (chmod 000) does not fail when running as root and is less portable. Use file-where-directory-expected.

STUCK GATE: progress only comes from the first write of a path in this attempt, or a check going fail->pass (worker.mjs:277,306). barren += 1 on every turn with a write, CHECK or DONE (342-343), and 4 means stuck. After both files have been written once, you get about 2-3 more write+check exchanges to turn a failing check into a passing one. Think before writing; do not make exploratory edits.

OUTPUT CAP: 16000 output tokens per reply (models.mjs:63). Writing a roughly 12k-char module and a 20k-char test file plus long reasoning in one reply risks truncation (doneReason 'length'). Write the module in one exchange and the tests in the next. Each counts as progress.

Self-review checkpoints withhold DONE: a write over 12000 chars (worker.mjs:280), a new SUBTASK index (244), a check flip (307-310) or the same failure twice (312-315) makes the NEXT exchange a checkpoint. Budget one exchange to re-run CHECK before DONE. Do not change SUBTASK labels needlessly.

Adding exported helpers that nothing uses. The worker system prompt forbids unreferenced additions (worker-system.md:145-148), and reviewers flag them. Export only installDisabledAutomation (plus task 1's verifyDisabledSchedule).

Deleting or consuming root/proposed/<name>.json, or editing scripts/orion-automation, schedule.mjs (including its nextGate text) or any runtime module. All are out of scope, and the boundary refuses the write anyway.
exchangePlan: Exchange 1: ### SUBTASK 1/3 read the interfaces. READ exactly these six files in one reply: scripts/lib/orion-automation-schedule.mjs, scripts/lib/orion-automation-dispatch.mjs, scripts/lib/orion-automation-admission.mjs, scripts/lib/orion-automation-runtime.mjs, tests/automation-schedule.test.mjs, tests/automation-runtime.test.mjs. The two scope files are already in the working set. Do not read more; a 9th file evicts the install module.

Exchange 2: Re-read task 1's code in the working set: the exact verifyDisabledSchedule signature, its helpers, and every existing test. Write down (briefly, in prose) the record fields, the transaction states and the call order. No writes yet if you are unsure; reading turns do not count toward the stuck gate.

Exchange 3: ### SUBTASK 2/3 implement. ### FILE scripts/lib/orion-automation-install.mjs: the COMPLETE file, with task 1's code unchanged plus installDisabledAutomation and local durable-write helpers. Then ### CHECK. The existing task 1 tests should still pass. This is a new write, so it counts as progress.

Exchange 4: This is probably a self-review checkpoint (large write or subtask change), and DONE would be withheld anyway. Read the check output. If node-syntax or the task 1 tests fail, fix the module and ### CHECK.

Exchange 5: ### SUBTASK 3/3 tests. ### FILE tests/automation-install.test.mjs: the COMPLETE file, with every task 1 test kept plus: success; 8-way same-name concurrency via allSettled; existing installed record unchanged; existing transaction refused; failure before create (invalid input and root as a regular file); failed read-back (mismatch and read throws); publication failure (root/runtime as a regular file); missing required arguments. Then ### CHECK.

Exchanges 6-8: Fix only what the failure output names. Each exchange: one complete FILE, then ### CHECK. If the same failure repeats twice, stop editing and re-read the relevant module in the working set (for example dispatch.mjs for binding). The stuck gate trips after about 3 non-progress write/check turns.

Exchange 9: Once all three checks pass: self-review against each of the 5 acceptance criteria and the non-scope (no child_process, no homedir, no enable, no remove call, intent written 'wx' before create, id persisted before read, same object for ledger and installed file). Fix anything found, then ### CHECK.

Exchange 10: ### DONE with a one-paragraph mapping from each criterion to the test that proves it. If DONE is withheld by a checkpoint, run ### CHECK again with no edits, then ### DONE on the next exchange.
Exchanges 11-14: Reserve. If the checks cannot be made to pass, or a required change lies outside the two scope files, reply ### BLOCKED with the exact failing assertion and what was tried.
reviewerChecks: Criterion 1: the diff exports installDisabledAutomation with the destructured {root,proposal,timeZone,repoRoot,scheduler,now}. It throws before any fs or scheduler effect when root, repoRoot or a scheduler method is missing. It has no homedir(), no default path, no child_process/execFile/spawn import, and never calls anything on scheduler except createDisabled and read (not remove, not enable). Tests assert that the plan passed to createDisabled deepEquals an independently computed automationSchedulePlan(...) and contains '--disabled'. What false compliance looks like: `root = join(homedir(), ...)` defaults, or tests that never exercise the missing-argument paths.

Criterion 2: the record includes name = proposal.name (not plan.name), trigger, timeZone, installationId from randomUUID() (not 'preview-only' or a constant), installedAt as an ISO string from `now`, and plan.policy fields. The call is initializeAutomationDispatch(join(root,'runtime'), record), and the installed file is join(root,'installed', `${proposal.name}.json`). The SAME object is written to both; there is no later mutation. What false compliance looks like: hand-written ledger JSON, extra fields added to the installed file only (the runtime would refuse with invalid_state), or tests that assert the file exists but never parse its fields or check the dispatch ledger.

Criterion 3: the intent is created with an exclusive open ('wx' flag) and fsynced BEFORE the createDisabled call. schedulerId is persisted durably (write, rename, directory sync) BEFORE scheduler.read is called. The installed record is published exclusively (wx or link, not rename). No code path unlinks or overwrites an existing intent. Tests read the transaction file inside the fake adapters at call time. What false compliance looks like: a check-then-write without wx, the id written after verification, or an intent file that holds only the id and not the plan and record that task 3 needs.

Criterion 4: the success value is returned only after the ledger and installed-record writes and a verifyDisabledSchedule(plan, observed) === true on read(id) output. Each failure path writes a distinguishable durable state. Before create: no file, or a no-effect marker. Create threw or gave an invalid id: unknown. Id known with read-back failed: evidence kept, not labeled disabled. Publication failed: the known verified job recorded. Tests assert on-disk state after each failure. What false compliance looks like: a catch-all that returns {status:'failed'} with nothing on disk, success returned before publication, or remove() called on mismatch.

Criterion 5: the test file contains all six named cases plus every task 1 test, unchanged or strengthened. Concurrency: exactly one verified result and exactly one createDisabled call. Existing record: byte-for-byte equality, and no create call. Failed read-back: observed built from literals with one field altered, not derived from the plan the fake received. Publication failure: injected through the real fs, e.g. root/runtime as a regular file, with no installed record afterwards. Any runInstalledAutomation call passes automationRoot, repoRoot, checks and run. What false compliance looks like: a fake read that echoes the plan, a concurrency test that runs calls sequentially, or a 'failure before create' test where the scheduler was never wired, so zero calls proves nothing.

Whole-diff checks: only the two scope files changed. verifyDisabledSchedule's export and behavior are unchanged. No existing test was weakened or deleted. No new unreferenced exports. No ENOENT or 'No such file or directory' text in test titles. The check output shows node-syntax, automation-install-tests and automation-tests all PASSED, with none UNUSABLE. The checks.mjs automation-tests suite list is untouched (it cannot be touched anyway: it is outside scope).
